title: Relative finite presentation coincides with absolute over a finitely presentable base map, and detects the base map itself
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
difficulty_reason: For f : X -> S locally of finite type and a quasi-coherent module F, the lemma states (1) if f is locally of finite presentation then F is finitely presented relative to S exactly when F is (absolutely) finitely presented, and (2) f is locally of finite presentation iff O_X is finitely presented relative to S — the dictionary pinning the relative notion to the absolute one and recovering the morphism property from the structure module. The retained proof is written as the definitional unfolding the author signs with Follows immediately from the definitions plus a pointer to the discussion following More on Algebra, definition relatively-finitely-presented — that discussion records exactly the two identifications (relative presentations over an affine base restrict to ordinary finite presentations once the base algebra is itself finitely presented; and O_X's relative presentation of length one is the finite-presentation data of the structure sheaf), so the lemma is the labeled export of that dictionary. Retained author proof at lines 16465-16470.
